applied.problem: "Any vector can be split into two parts" is false for the 3-D vectors this same lesson and the cross product (i6) use, which need three parts, i, j and k; narrowed to a vector on a flat page.
The worked example check writes √(4² + 6.93²) = √64, but 16 + 6.93² is 64.02; the rounded part only gives back 8 knots to rounding, so the equals sign is false precision.
